ruling.reasoning:
The rider complains the driver left the app's route and the meter exceeded the estimate [F1][F2], and the driver says he diverted around an accident on the Seletar Expressway [F10]. The trace settles one off-route segment, 17:38–17:49, 6.56 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.64 km, +4.92 km [F3], so RD-1 is engaged and the segment must be tested against RD-4 [RD-1].

The driver's "reasonable cause" claim is not taken on his word: it is corroborated by a traffic fact. An accident on the Seletar Expressway (towards TPE) after Woodlands Avenue 12 Exit was reported at 17:16, located 0 m from the optimal route, and lies within 300 m of optimal-route km 7.1–8.7 — the stretch the detour replaced [F13]. The report (17:16) precedes the segment's start (17:38) and the trip window (17:28–18:01), and the segment's up-to-1911 m displacement is consistent with routing around that point [F3]. RD-4(a)'s conditions therefore hold, and this segment is exempt [RD-4]. The speed-band records for Seletar and Tampines Expressways [F11][F12] are not needed and, per RD-4(b), would not exempt a segment on their own [RD-4].

Because the only off-route segment is exempt, there is no non-exempt detour distance to refund: Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments = 0, so the formula in the trace yields 0 × $1.4099/km = $0.00 — no_action, not refund_partial [F3][F6][RD-2]. I note for completeness that even the billed excess shown separately ($7.19 = 5.10 km × $1.4099/km) [F4] is distance-fare on a RydeTAXI meter [F6]; since the segment that produced the extra distance is exempt, no part of it is refundable under RD-2 [RD-2].

The consent route is not reached: RD-5 is only a fallback where RD-4 does not already excuse the segment, and here it does [F3][RD-5]. No rider-requested stop is recorded either: the only messages are the rider's 17:23 pickup note and the driver's 17:24 reply, both timestamped [F7][F8][F9], so RD-3 does not apply [RD-3].

RD-6's extra action is not triggered: the driver's profile shows 2 upheld disputes but route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so this case does not make a repeated route breach [F16][RD-6]. Profile facts play no part in deciding the fare itself [F15][F16].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the two chat messages and the driver's statement in full. The messages are a pickup arrangement ("main entrance, grey hoodie") and an arrival estimate ("about 4 min, white Honda Vezel") [F7][F8]; the driver's statement is a route explanation [F10]; the complaint is a fare grievance. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Safety concern: none.

Evidence is sufficient: the off-route segment is measured [F3], the fare record shows the distance fare and distance used for the rate [F4][F6], the traffic incident is placed on the replaced stretch with a timestamp [F13], and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F9]. Every element my ruling needs is on the record, so no gap is named and no escalation is required.
